claims.text: The investigated alloy is eutectic AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The as-cast alloy has a fine lamellar dual-phase fcc/B2 microstructure.
The initial inter-lamellar spacing is approximately 2 μm.
At room temperature, the as-cast alloy has an engineering fracture stress of about 944 MPa and elongation of about 25.6%.
The alloy suffers catastrophic interfacial cracking and stress concentration at fcc/B2 phase boundaries during room-temperature uniaxial tension.
Extreme-pressure severe plastic deformation will convert the continuous lamellar fcc/B2 structure into a fragmented, patterned, or equiaxed nanostructure without changing bulk composition.
Suitable treatment parameters are HPT above 5 GPa or high-pressure extrusion above 1 GPa at 400–600 °C.
A temperature of 400–600 °C will facilitate dynamic recovery or recrystallization while preserving phase stability.
Pressure above 5 GPa will suppress void formation and promote dense plastic flow.
A high strain rate will cause shear localization and lamellar breakup.
The treatment will produce nanoscale or equiaxed grains with high-angle grain boundaries and a reduced B2-phase aspect ratio.
Extreme hydrostatic pressure suppresses void nucleation and coalescence at phase interfaces.
Severe plastic deformation induces shear bands that fragment the lamellae.
The refined, grain-boundary-rich microstructure promotes uniform dislocation glide and strain hardening.
After HITMT, room-temperature tensile elongation will exceed 35%.
After HITMT, fracture stress will exceed 1000 MPa.
Fragmenting the continuous B2 pathways will arrest interfacial cracking and make plastic deformation more uniform.
Successful processing requires remaining below melting and avoiding phase decomposition, substantial changes in the fcc/B2 ratio, and excessive grain growth.
Pressure must remain below a level that would transform the alloy into an amorphous state.
HIP at 1400 °C and 200 MPa for 2 hours is a conventional densification treatment suitable as the comparison condition.

contradictions.description: The intervention permits high-pressure extrusion above 1 GPa, whereas the conditions state that pressure must exceed 5 GPa, leaving the applicable minimum pressure inconsistent.

The proposed result—HIP failing while extreme-pressure SPD succeeds—would support rather than falsify a claim that extreme pressure or pressure-assisted deformation is necessary. In addition, HIP and HITMT differ in temperature, pressure, and imposed strain, so this comparison does not isolate extreme pressure.
